chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'All goodness is tied in the forelocks of the cavalry horses until the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'goodness is tied in the forelocks of the horses' mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that all goodness is tied to the forelocks of cavalry horses until the Day of Judgment, a tradition frequently cited by Shia scholars to highlight the enduring spiritual merit of jihad and military readiness. This narration underscores the physical preparation for battle as a conduit for divine favor, linking the tangible act of maintaining warhorses with the eternal reward of striving in God's path.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba, from Ma’mar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The goodness, all of it is tied up in the forelocks of the cavalry horse, up to the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah from Mu’ammar who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say the following:
‘All of goodness is written on the foreheads of the horses to remain up to the Day of Judgment.’”
